papers.title: Isolation of Toxoplasma gondii-specific IgG and mass spectrometric characterization of individual IgGs for early diagnosis of toxoplasmosis
papers.abstract: Objectives: Toxoplasmosis represents a significant global health burden, particularly among immunocompromised patients and newborns of mothers who contracted a primary infection during pregnancy. In the newborn, maternally transferred Toxoplasma gondii-specific IgG persist for up to six months and mask the IgG newly synthesized by the infant, delaying diagnosis. Individual polymor-phisms of the IgG heavy chain constant region (IGHG) can distinguish the two origins, but have so far been characterized only in total circulating IgG. We assessed whether this discrimination can be achieved on the IgG fraction directed against the parasite itself. Methods: Recombinant T. gondii antigens (TgSAG1, TgGRA7, TgAMA1) were produced and evaluated by ELISA on 85 seropositive and 95 seronegative plasma samples. Parasite-specific IgG were then immunopurified from a mixture of plasma from two donors, one seropositive and one seronegative, carrying distinct IGHG1 and IGHG3 alleles known from DNA sequencing, and their Fc/2 fragments were analyzed by middle-down and bottom-up LC-MS/MS. Results: TgSAG1 proved the most effective antigen; combined with TgAMA1 and/or TgGRA7 it reached 100% sensitivity and 97% specificity. Middle-down analysis offered high specificity but insufficient sensitivity for the microliter plasma volumes required in newborns. Bottom-up analysis identified the peptide WQQGNVFSCSVMHEGLHNHYTQK, characteristic of IGHG1*07, exclusively in the seropositive donor, in agreement with DNA sequencing data. Conclusion: Combining antigen-affinity immunopurification with IGHG proteotyping allows an individual IGHG allele to be assigned within a pathogen-specific polyclonal IgG fraction representing less than 0.5% of total plasma IgG. This first demonstration, obtained in a two-donor context, opens the way to distinguishing maternal from fetal specific IgG for the early diagnosis of congenital toxoplasmosis.

papers.title: Fit-for-purpose bioanalytical validation of a three-cytokine human PBMC ELISpot panel (IFN-γ, IL-2, IL-4) using CEFX and CPI antigen pools for clinical trial immunomonitoring under a GLP-aligned quality system
papers.abstract: Cellular immunity is an increasingly required endpoint in clinical trials of vaccines, immuno-oncology agents, and cell therapies. Multi-cytokine validation packages under a single quality system remain uncommon, and the permissible interval between blood draw and plating or freezing is rarely demonstrated experimentally. We performed GLP-aligned, fit-for-purpose validation of three human peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) ELISpot assays, following Global CRO Council recommendations and FDA, NMPA, and CFDI guidance. IFN-gamma and IL-2 were stimulated with CEFX Ultra SuperStim Pool (24 h each, plus a validated 48 h IFN-gamma regimen) and IL-4 with CPI Antigen Pool (CTL-CPI-001; 48 h) throughout all validation arms. We characterized limit of detection (LOD), lower limit of quantification (LLOQ), precision, linearity across six plating densities, robustness, pre-analytical PBMC functional stability under five delayed-processing conditions in fresh and cryopreserved arms. All assays met predefined criteria (>=80% of samples with %CV =0.97); LOD/LLOQ were 13/20 and 37/45 SFU/well for IFN-gamma at 24 h and 48 h, 9/27 for IL-2, and 4/27 for IL-4. Freshly plated PBMC remained within acceptance after up to 8 h plus 24 h of ambient holding, whereas cryopreservation after prolonged delay failed at 8+16 h for IL-2 and IL-4 and at 8+24 h for all three assays, driven by post-thaw viability less than 80%. These data define evidence-based sample-handling windows for multicenter trials. The resulting three-cytokine platform is fit-for-purpose for regulated clinical immunomonitoring.

papers.title: Cross-neutralization of Bundibugyo virus following Ebola virus booster vaccination
papers.abstract: Background: The ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) highlights the absence of a licensed Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) vaccine. Ebola virus (EBOV) vaccines can induce cross-reactive BDBV binding antibodies, but evidence of cross-neutralizing antibodies is limited. Methods: In the EBO-BOOST trial (NCT06126822), previously EBOV-vaccinated adults received an ERVEBO booster after primary vaccination with ERVEBO (E|E, n=60) or ZABDENO/MVABEA (Zm|E, n=40). Neutralizing antibodies against EBOV and BDBV were measured at baseline, day 21 (D21) and month 6 (M6) using biologically contained EBOV-dVP30-eGFP and BDBV-dVP30-eGFP reporter viruses. Results: BDBV seropositivity increased from 8% at baseline to 67% at D21, declining to 34% at M6. Median NT50 titers were significantly lower for BDBV than for EBOV at D21 (40.9 vs 244.1; P<0.001) and at M6 (<20 vs 66.5; P<0.001). In mixed-effects models adjusted for time since primary vaccination, BDBV responses were 65% lower than EBOV responses at D21 (GMR 0.35; 95% CI 0.26-0.48) and 50% lower at M6 (GMR 0.50; 95% CI 0.40-0.63). The Zm|E group showed a higher BDBV fold change from baseline at D21 than the E|E group (GMR 1.75; p=0.023). Conclusions: An ERVEBO booster induces BDBV cross-neutralizing antibodies in most recipients, but responses are lower than against EBOV and largely wane by 6 months. Although protective significance and correlates of protection remain to be established, these findings support evaluation of ERVEBO in parallel with BDBV-specific vaccines.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling reveals venom-specific T-cells associated with tolerance during immunotherapy
papers.abstract: BackgroundVenom immunotherapy (VIT) is well established, but the dynamics of the rare venom-specific T cells during treatment need to be investigated. Defining these responses may identify biomarkers and pathways associated with treatment-induced tolerance. MethodsWe sampled nine wasp-allergic individuals before and 7 days and 6 months after initiation of VIT, and 5 non-allergic donors at one time point. Single-cell RNA sequencing of isolated venom-specific T cells was used to characterise changes to immunophenotypes and immune receptor repertoires during VIT. ResultsWe unveiled a broad phenotype diversity among venom-specific T cells, which were altered during VIT. Most notably, IL5Th2 cells strongly correlated with Ves v 5-specific IgE levels at baseline, whereas their increase during VIT was associated with protective humoral immune responses, determined by the Ves v 5-specific IgG4/IgE ratio. Moreover, VIT induced exhaustion markers in Tconv, whereas Tregs acquired an activated phenotype, which was associated with increased specific IgG4 levels. T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire analysis revealed a highly polyclonal repertoire and substantial clonal expansion and plasticity in Tconv. By contrast, Treg clonotypes emerged during VIT, with no evidence of Tconv-to-Treg conversion. ConclusionVIT induces early phenotypic changes in venom-specific T cells, which are associated with a protective IgG4 response. In particular, IL5Th2 and activated Tregs may represent candidate biomarkers of both antigen-specific sensitisation and VIT response and suggest a potential role of IL-5-related pathways in allergen-specific tolerance development. Furthermore, Tconv and Tregs TCR repertoires remained separated during VIT, opposing the Tconv-to-Treg transition hypothesis. papers.title: Detection of Peanut Allergy Sensitization and Monitoring of Type 2 Memory B cells Using Recombinant Peanut Allergen Components
papers.abstract: Background Peanut allergy is one of the most common causes of life-threatening food allergy, and therefore the focus of multiple clinical trials for allergen immunotherapy. Diagnosis relies on detection of allergen-specific serum IgE, which provides limited information on severity and threshold. Furthermore, objective biomarkers to predict allergic persistence and efficacy of treatment are lacking. Therefore, we aimed to incorporate recombinant peanut allergen components in a multiplex Cytometric Basophil detection assay (CytoBas) for detection of peanut sensitization, and in a memory B cell (Bmem) panel for evaluation of biomarkers of disease. Methods In 27 adult peanut-allergic patients, allergen-specific IgE levels were determined by ImmunoCAP, and component-specific IgE by ELISA. PBMC of all patients and of 15 non-sensitized controls were analyzed by flow cytometry with basophil markers and six fluorochrome-conjugated allergen component tetramers for CytoBas, while circulating Bmem were studied including fluorescent tetramers for Ara h 1, Ara h 2 and Ara h 3. Results CytoBas demonstrated similar-to-improved diagnostic performance compared to IgE ELISAs for Ara h -1, -2, -3, -6, -8 allergens (ROCs AUC 0.79-1.0 versus 0.78-0.9). Ara h 2 discriminated all patients from controls, while combined Ara h 1, 3 and 6 (excluding major allergen Ara h 2) elicited 78-81% sensitivity with 100% specificity. Peanut-allergic patients showed expansion of the pathogenic Type 2 Bmem subset within Ara h 1-, 2- and 3-specific cells, and the Ara h 1+ and Ara h 3+ Bmem contained expanded IgG4+ and IgG1 subsets. Conclusions Peanut CytoBas displays similar to superior diagnostic accuracy to component-specific IgE serology, enabling efficient evaluation of multiple allergen components in a single test tube. Peanut-allergic individuals show increased frequencies of allergen-specific type 2 Bmem, which could be longitudinally evaluated to monitor the natural course of disease or allergen immunotherapy.

papers.title: Single-cell dissection of immune-state architecture across diverse human population cohorts
papers.abstract: The extension of human lifespan is accompanied by a growing burden of chronic disease and multimorbidity. The immune system, whose functional state is continuously remodelled by ageing, environmental exposures, infection history and disease, is pivotal to respond to these challenges. However, how these factors jointly influence immune variation, regulatory mechanisms and disease susceptibility across populations remains poorly understood. Here we present an outline and first results of the CARDINAL (Cellular Architecture of immune-state Regulation, Disease, and Immune Networks across the Adult Lifecourse) project. We generated a new population-scale single-cell atlas of peripheral blood comprising almost 10 million immune cells from 6,003 individuals across two UK cohorts with integrated genomic and longitudinal electronic health record data: the UK Biobank (predominantly European ancestry British) and Genes & Health (British Bangladeshi and British Pakistani). We identify immune-state architectures, shared across cohorts, associated with ageing, chronic viral exposure, inflammatory activation and premalignant conditions. We show that demographic and lifestyle factors induce largely conserved immune programmes, while chronic cardiometabolic diseases are associated with cohort-dominant cellular programmes and transcriptional states. Disentangling of genetic and clinical influences reveals coordinated regulatory programmes associated with metabolic, inflammatory and infectious remodelling. These programmes are observed in specific disease contexts and immune states, such as those induced by chronic viral exposure, often independently of genetic differences. Together, our findings support a model of immune-state architecture shaped by ageing, environment, disease history and genetic variation, which can be read from population-specific regulatory landscapes.

papers.title: Broader functional and memory antibody responses in adult females than males in response to seasonal H3N2 vaccine virus
papers.abstract: Females of reproductive ages often mount greater antibody responses than males following influenza vaccination, but the breadth and depth of these differences, including antibody-dependent Fc receptor (FcR)-mediated functions have not been explored. Plasma samples were collected from male and female healthcare workers (range of 21-48y; mean of 31y) at 0, 28, and 180 days post-vaccination (DPV) during the 2022-2023 influenza vaccine season to assess antibody responses to A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria vaccine viruses. Females had greater A/H3N2, but not A/H1N1 or B/Victoria, neutralizing antibody (nAb) responses compared to males through 180 DPV, with differences being most pronounced among A/H3N2 responders ([≥]4 fold-change in nAb titers). Memory B cells isolated from female responders secreted more IgG in response to ex vivo H3 stimulation than those from male responders at 28 and 180 DPV. Before vaccination, female responders had greater anti-H3 IgG responses and Fc{gamma}RIIB (CD32b) antibody binding than males, with females maintaining greater responses through 180 DPV. Female responders had greater H3-specific antibody-dependent monocyte phagocytosis (ADMP) and natural killer cell (ADNK) secretion of IFN{gamma} and CCL4 prior to and after vaccination, with ADMP positively correlating with greater H3N2 neutralization through 180 DPV in females only. Among responders, the durability of ADMP, ADNK, and nAb in females as compared to males defined the sex differences in influenza-vaccine induced immunity. The greater Fc{gamma}R-binding antibodies prior to vaccination in females might improve the durability of both neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibody responses to diverse vaccines, including next generation influenza vaccines.

papers.title: Efficacy of an early first dose of whole-cell pertussis vaccine in infants for the prevention of IgE-mediated food allergy: A randomised controlled trial
papers.abstract: BackgroundEvidence from mechanistic and observational studies suggests that replacing the first acellular pertussis (aP) vaccine dose in early infancy with a whole-cell pertussis (wP)-containing vaccine may reduce the risk of developing IgE-mediated food allergy during childhood. ObjectiveWe aimed to determine if a dose of wP at approximately 6 weeks old, in lieu of aP vaccine, could reduce the incidence of food allergy in infants. MethodsIn this multicentre, randomised, participant and outcome assessor-blinded, parallel, two-stage, Bayesian adaptive trial we assigned Australian infants to one of two pertussis vaccination schedules. These consisted of either a standard homologous priming with a hexavalent combination aP vaccine (diphtheria, tetanus, aP, hepatitis B, inactivated poliovirus types 1, 2, and 3, and Haemophilus influenzae type b; DTaP-HepB-IPV-Hib) at approximately 6 weeks, 4 months and 6 months old ( aP-only schedule), or a first dose of a WHO-prequalified pentavalent wP combination vaccine (DTwP-HepB-Hib; Pentabio(R), PT Bio Farma Indonesia) at approximately 6 weeks old, followed by hexavalent aP combination vaccine at approximately 4 months and 6 months old ( mixed wP/aP schedule). The primary outcome was physician-confirmed food allergy by age 12 months requiring both evidence of sensitisation and compatible symptoms in response to either incidental or medically supervised oral food challenge. The initial target sample size was 3,000 enrolments to provide approximately 85% power to detect a policy-relevant 3 percentage point reduction in the risk of the primary outcome. ResultsA total of 972 infants were enrolled, 486 in each study arm. Of these, 26 of 486 (5.3%) assigned to the aP-only group and 31 of 486 (6.4%) assigned to the mixed wP/aP schedule met the primary endpoint definition. The posterior median difference (95% credible interval) in food allergy among recipients of the mixed wP/aP schedule compared to recipients of the aP-only schedule was 0.01 (-0.02, 0.04; probability [<0] 0.25). There were six serious adverse events (SAEs) among children receiving the aP-only group versus 12 among children receiving the mixed wP/aP schedule; one SAE (hospitalisation for irritability; length of stay < 48 hours) was deemed related to wP vaccine. The trial was stopped early owing to operational reasons. ConclusionsThere is a low probability of a policy-relevant reduction in food allergy in infants receiving mixed wP/aP versus aP-only pertussis vaccine schedules. Funded by the National Health and Medical Research Council of Australia; ANZCTR number, ACTRN12617000065392p. Clinical implicationsAn early first dose of wP is unlikely to afford a policy-relevant reduction in the probability of developing food allergy, eczema or atopic sensitisation in infants. Capsule summaryAn early first dose of a 5-in-1 wP combination vaccine is reasonably tolerated but would not be expected to have a material impact on the prevalence of food allergy in infants.

papers.title: Immune Defense Protein IDP Improves Cough and Chest Congestion During Cold and Flu Season in Older Adults: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundUpper respiratory infections are common and carry a greater burden in older adults. IDP(R) (Immune Defense Protein) is a dietary supplement whose active ingredient is a complex of milk-derived bioactive whey proteins. Prior studies of IDP(R) report enhanced antibody response following influenza vaccination, suggesting a potential for reduction of incidence, duration, and severity of upper respiratory symptoms. This study evaluated the effects of IDP(R) supplementation on the incidence, type, duration, and severity of upper respiratory symptoms in older adults during cold and flu season, along with rescue medication use and quality of life. MethodsThis was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study with three arms (placebo, standard dose of 50mg IDP(R) /day, and advanced dose of 200mg IDP(R) /day). Participants completed a one-week baseline period followed by a 16-week product use period, reporting daily upper respiratory symptoms via the Wisconsin Upper Respiratory Symptom Survey (WURSS-24). Participants additionally logged quality of life using the Short Form 36 (SF-36). ANCOVA for change from baseline, mixed models for repeated measures (MRMM), as well as Kruskal Wallis (KW) tests of area under the curve of symptom frequency and severity were used to compare trajectories over time. ResultsN=255 participants (n=88 Placebo, n=85 50 mg IDP(R), n=82 200 mg IDP(R)) were evaluated. Analysis of individual symptom trends over time revealed that chest congestion and cough decreased in severity and duration significantly faster in the 50 mg IDP(R) and 200 mg IDP(R) groups compared to Placebo (KW for Area Under the Curve p 0.05). SF-36 quality of life did not differ between arms. Adverse events potentially attributable to product use were infrequent, resolved, and did not differ between arms. ConclusionsSixteen weeks of daily IDP(R) supplementation was associated with a reduction in duration and severity of cough and chest congestion in older adults. IDP(R) appears safe and tolerable. Trial RegistrationThe trial was reviewed and approved by BeyondBound IRB: BB2511NC-152, and registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT07431840)

papers.title: Digital cytometry of immune cell types from dried blood microsamples
papers.abstract: Enumeration of circulating immune cells is an established clinical practice implemented across a plethora of indications. While flow cytometry is the gold standard for this task, cellular deconvolution algorithms provide a robust computational alternative using molecular data. These digital cytometry pipelines typically rely on millilitre-scale venous blood samples. Here, we evaluated the potential of capillary blood microsampling as a patient-centric and minimally invasive approach for the digital cytometry of major lymphocyte populations (T cells, B cells, and natural killer cells; TBNK). In a cohort of 200 participants, we compared RNA sequencing based deconvolution performance between matched PAXgene-stabilised venous blood and Mitra capillary blood microsamples. While venous transcriptomes enabled highly accurate TBNK estimation, patient-matched capillary microsamples exhibited a significant reduction in deconvolution accuracy. Computational adaptations, including the integration of capillary-specific single-cell reference profiles, yielded only limited improvements. Instead, our analyses revealed that the performance deficit was primarily driven by the decreased transcriptome complexity of the capillary microsample libraries. This study highlights the critical role of transcript diversity for cellular deconvolution and reveals the current pre-analytical challenges that must be overcome to harness transcriptomics based digital cytometry using dried blood microsamples.

papers.title: Quantifying age-associated differences in the durability of Shingrix-induced immunity using mathematical modelling
papers.abstract: Understanding the durability of vaccine-induced immunity is critical for evaluating long-term protection and vaccine scheduling, particularly in aging populations where immunosenescence may alter immune response dynamics. In this study, we used a novel mathematical modelling pipeline to quantify age-related differences in the contraction and persistence phases of gE-specific CD4+ T cell and anti-gE antibody responses following Shingrix vaccination. Specifically, we developed a semi-mechanistic model to expand virtual populations that captured inter-individual variability in peak concentrations and waning dynamics. To compare immune responses across age groups, we introduced a time varying, age-related immune advantage metric that measures the probability of a randomly selected younger individual exhibiting a stronger immune response than one from an older group. By evaluating this metric across multiple simulated virtual populations, our results demonstrate clear and sustained age-related differences in both gE-specific CD4+ T cells and anti-gE antibody responses, with younger age groups consistently exhibiting higher responses. Given these age-related differences, we used our model to explore alternative vaccine schedules in older age groups. These exploratory simulations suggest that booster doses administered between 6 and 12 months following the second dose may mitigate age-related differences in antibody dynamics. This work highlights the use of mechanistic mathematical modelling to disentangle age-associated differences in vaccine outcomes and lead to designing of plausible improvement in age-specific vaccine schedules.

papers.title: Dysregulated B Cell Education Drives Autoimmunity and Immunodeficiency in Down Syndrome
papers.abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) present with both increased rates of autoimmunity and immunodeficiency. To understand this paradox, we first examined lymph node (LN) architecture and immune cell composition in infants with and without DS, as well as peripheral blood B cells from unrelated adults with and without DS. Most strikingly, LNs from individuals with DS exhibited a marked paucity of germinal centers compared with typical lymph nodes. Stromal cells within DS LNs expressed significantly lower levels of the adhesion molecules ICAM1 and VCAM1, accompanied by significantly reduced CXCR5 expression within B cell follicles, suggesting impaired B cell migration and follicular organization. Although fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) were present at comparable frequencies in DS and control LNs, MARCO lymphatic endothelial cells (MARCO-LECs), another critical stromal cell population supporting LN architecture, were significantly reduced. In addition, follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), which are essential for antigen retention and B cell selection within germinal centers, were also substantially reduced. To determine the consequences of these abnormalities on humoral immunity, we performed paired single-cell RNA sequencing and V(D)J sequencing of peripheral blood B cells from adults with and without DS. DS memory and CD86+ switched memory B cell populations exhibited significantly elevated reactive oxygen species and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling gene signatures, coupled with reduced levels of somatic hypermutation in the memory population and increase usage of the autoreactivity-associated IGHV4-34 heavy-chain gene. Collectively, these findings suggest that early-life disruption of LN architecture, characterized by reduced expression of adhesion molecules, selective loss of MARCO-LECs, and depletion of FDCs, impairs germinal center function and B cell education. This defective microenvironment likely contributes to inadequate affinity maturation, as reflected by diminished somatic hypermutation and a more autoreactive B cell repertoire in adults with Down syndrome.

papers.title: Gamma delta T cells are expanded in the blood of chronic low back pain patients with lumbar Modic changes
papers.abstract: ObjectivesModic changes (MC) are vertebral endplate and bone marrow lesions strongly associated with chronic low back pain. Type 1 MC (MC1, oedema-like) and type 2 or 3 MC (MC2or3, fat- and sclerosis-like) are commonly regarded as different stages of the same pathological process, yet their underlying biology remains poorly defined. In particular, it remains unclear whether MC are confined to the spine or accompanied by distinct systemic immune alterations. Here, we provide the first comprehensive characterisation of the circulating immune landscape in patients with lumbar MC. MethodsPeripheral blood mononuclear cells were analysed from 37 patients undergoing lumbar spinal surgery: 11 with no MC, 15 with MC1 and 11 with MC2or3. Samples were fluorescently barcoded, pooled, and stained with a 28-antibody phenotyping panel. Each pool was then split into 30 aliquots, and each of these was co-stained with a different PE-conjugated anti-integrin, -selectin, or -chemokine receptor antibody or isotype controls. Differences in abundance were tested with binomial mixed models adjusted for acquisition batch, age, and sex. Differentially abundant compartments were clustered by FlowSOM and the same binomial model was used to test differences in cluster abundance. Adhesion receptors were analysed as single chains. ResultsThe {gamma}{delta} T cell compartment was the only population significantly expanded in MC patients (median 0.58% of all recorded cells in nonMC donors versus 1.61% in pooled MC (OR = 2.38, q = 0.035)). Clustering {gamma}{delta} T cells into subsets showed compartment-wide expansion, primarily driven by V{delta}2+ T cells. The adhesion receptor screen revealed 6 and 2 integrin on basophils, endoglin on plasmacytoid dendritic cells, and {beta}7 integrin on IgA B cells as differentially expressed in MC, but none survived multiple-testing correction across the whole screen. ConclusionsLumbar MC are accompanied by expansion of circulating {gamma}{delta} T cells. This aligns with previously reported {gamma}{delta} T cell accumulation in MC1 lesions, underscoring the role of {gamma}{delta} T cells in MC pathophysiology.

papers.title: Exploring the Barriers and Facilitators of Vaccine Procurement in Health Districts of the South West Region of Cameroon
papers.abstract: BackgroundImmunization is the most cost-effective way of preventing vaccine-preventable diseases and reducing morbidity and mortality in children 0 to 5 years old. The vaccine procurement capacity of health districts significantly influences the vaccine coverage rates. The advent of the socio-political crisis in the North West and South West Regions of Cameroon could have had a negative bearing on vaccine procurement and thus coverage rates. Thus, this study was carried out to explore the barriers and facilitators of vaccine procurement in health districts of a South West Region of Cameroon. This will help reduce vaccine stock-out at the health district level and increase vaccine coverage. MethodologyA qualitative study was conducted using in-depth interviews (IDIs) to collect data from healthcare providers in all the 21 health districts in the South West Region working with the Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI), and who met the inclusion criteria. A Delphi consensus approach was employed to formulate feasible facilitators to the optimization of vaccine procurement. Data was analysed using Nvivo 11. Thematic analysis was used to explore the barriers to vaccine procurement at the level of health districts. A Delphi consensus of [≥] 70.0% was considered acceptable. ResultsFrom the thematic analysis, nine broad themes: financial constraints, limited workforce, inadequate transportation logistics, poor equipment, inadequate managerial skills, inadequate in-service training, vaccine stock-out and weak primary health care (PHC) system facilities emerged as barriers to vaccine procurement. Of the 12 strategies retained for the optimization of vaccine procurement, 5 (41.7%) were priority strategies: provision of extra solar refrigerators (100.0%), WHO certification training for EPI staff (100.0%), financial allocation for transport (100.0%), equipment and training, in-service training for both district and health facility staff (100.0%), resolving the socio-political crisis (100.0%) and provision of specialized transport logistics for maritime Health Districts (100.0%). ConclusionFinancing of vaccine procurement, recruitment/certification of staff, provision of transportation logistics, provision of solar refrigerators, regular supervision, organization of in-service training, with focus on requisition/stock and bulk-requisition were the main strategies suggested to overcome the barriers to vaccine procurement. RecommendationsThese findings highlight the need for all stakeholders to co-finance and manage vaccine procurement at the health district level in the South West Region of Cameroon.

papers.title: An early activated CD38highCD209highCD36low monocyte phenotype is associated with progression to severe dengue
authors: M. H. M. T. S. H. M. T. S. Perera
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlthough monocytes are among the principal target cells of dengue virus (DENV) infection we sought to investigate monocyte phenotypic markers associated with disease severity and evaluate their potential as prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. MethodsDifferences in monocyte subpopulations and phenotypic markers were assessed by flow cytometry in patients with dengue fever (DF=33) and dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF=21) and compared to health controls (HCs=20). Further in vitro experiments were done by co-culturing peripheral blood mononucleocytes (PBMCs) of healthy individuals (n=8) with DENV2, DENV3, NS1 antigen of both serotypes and LPS. The changes in expression of CD36 and CD38 in vitro in monocytes were assessed. ResultsA significant expansion of intermediate monocytes and a contraction of the classical monocytes was seen in patients with DHF compared to DF and HCs, with no significant differences within the non-classical monocytes. Patients who progressed to develop DHF, exhibited an activated monocyte phenotype characterized by, expansion of CD38high, CD209high, CD86high, HLA-DRhigh, CD36low, intermediate monocyte subset. The highest expression of CD38 and CD86 was seen in non-classical monocytes, and CD209 and HLA-DR in intermediate monocytes. Most significant downregulation of CD36 was observed in non-classical monocytes. CD38 expression on monocytes (especially classical monocytes) positively and significantly correlated with liver transaminases and serum ferritin levels. Co-culture of PBMCs with DENV3 led to significant downregulation of CD36 (p=0.023). ConclusionsThese results suggest that early alterations in monocyte activation, antigen presentation, viral entry, and lipid sensing pathways contribute to dengue immunopathogenesis.

papers.title: Dermal macrophages acquire a TREM2-anchored profibrotic state in antiphospholipid syndrome that is reflected in the circulation
papers.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a systemic autoimmune disease best known for thrombosis and obstetric morbidity. APS is sometimes also characterized by chronic microvascular disease, which can impair renal and other organ function. Skin offers an accessible window into the tissue mechanisms underlying such manifestations. Our previous single-cell analysis of skin biopsies from three patients with established microvascular disease focused on dermal endothelial cells and implicated a Hippo-YAP1-CCN2 axis in vascular pathology. Here, we expanded single-cell profiling to dermal tissue from 30 patients with primary APS and 14 age- and sex-matched healthy controls to characterize different tissue-resident cell states and their intercellular communication networks. Cellular composition was largely preserved. Disease-associated differences were centered on myeloid transcriptional states and predicted interactions with stromal cells. Dermal myeloid cells acquired a TREM2-anchored, lipid-associated program characterized by increased expression of genes involved in lipid handling and lysosomal function. These TREM2 macrophages were the major predicted source of profibrotic osteopontin and target of stromal apolipoprotein E signaling. Expression of this dermal program correlated positively with plasma soluble TREM2 and osteopontin, and all three measures correlated inversely with estimated glomerular filtration rate. Furthermore, soluble TREM2 was higher in APS patients with suspected or established nephropathy than in those without nephropathy. Together, these findings identify a tissue macrophage program in primary APS that is reflected in the circulation and associated with renal involvement, suggesting a role for macrophage-stromal interactions in chronic microvascular disease.

papers.title: Plasma Metabolomics During Chemotherapy Desensitization: A Pilot Study
papers.abstract: BackgroundRapid drug desensitization permits continued chemotherapy, but no validated blood measurement predicts breakthrough reactions during desensitization. ObjectiveTo compare paired plasma metabolomic and lipidomic changes during chemotherapy desensitization with those in tolerant controls, and to describe breakthrough and omalizumab encounters. MethodsIn this pilot study, 10 patients undergoing carboplatin or paclitaxel desensitization and four tolerant controls receiving standard infusions contributed 76 draws across 39 encounters (37 with paired pre- and post-infusion draws). Untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry in four modes yielded 8,646 quality-filtered features (instrument signals). Exact permutation with false discovery rate control compared patient-averaged paired changes from 27 allergic encounters (10 patients) off omalizumab with four control encounters (four patients). Breakthrough and omalizumab comparisons were descriptive. ResultsAllergic patients profiles changed from pre- to post-infusion in three of four modes (Holm-adjusted P = .04). Pre-infusion profiles differed between allergic patients and controls in one mode (Holm-adjusted P = .02). Montelukast, a premedication drug, had the smallest P value among annotated pre-infusion differences and was detected in all 33 allergic and no control pre-infusion draws. No feature distinguished allergic from control paired changes at a 5% false discovery rate. Histamine did not consistently increase in seven paired breakthrough encounters (five patients). Hemolysis was more frequent in allergic post-infusion than pre-infusion draws (16 of 35 vs eight of 33). ConclusionProfiling during desensitization detected premedication exposure and broad pre-to-post changes largely shared with controls, but no allergy-specific signature. Prospective studies need sampling timed to reactions and medications, comparators matched for premedication and infusion duration, and standardized specimen handling. Highlights BoxO_ST_ABSWhat is already known about this topic?C_ST_ABSDesensitization lets most patients with carboplatin or paclitaxel hypersensitivity continue treatment. Breakthrough reactions occur, and no validated blood measurement predicts them. What does this article add to our knowledge?In 14 patients, plasma profiling detected premedication signals before infusion and broad pre-to-post changes; no feature distinguished allergic from control changes at a 5% false discovery rate. Histamine did not consistently rise with breakthrough reactions. How does this study impact current management guidelines?Biomarker studies during chemotherapy desensitization should match comparators for premedication, time blood draws to symptom onset, and standardize specimen processing; these exploratory findings do not change current desensitization practice.

papers.title: Hierarchy of immunogenicity of Plasmodium falciparum merozoite antigens and vaccine candidates in first human infection
papers.abstract: BackgroundMerozoite antigens are targets of acquired immunity and are promising targets for next-generation malaria vaccines and serosurveillance tools. However, the immunogenicity of each antigen and their induction of antibodies following infection remains unclear, impacting vaccine design, antigen selection in serosurveillance, and our understanding of naturally-acquired immunity. MethodsTo address this, we assessed IgG and IgM responses to whole merozoites and individual merozoite antigens in 81 malaria-naive adults who experienced a blood-stage P. falciparum Controlled Human Malaria Infection (CHMI). ResultsSignificant acquisition of IgG and IgM against whole merozoites could be detected as early as two weeks after infection. For IgG responses, a strong hierarchy of immunogenicity among merozoite antigens was observed, with several prominent antigen targets. In contrast, IgM was acquired to most antigens and was less hierarchical with a broader and less antigen-dominant acquisition profile. Participants clustered into distinct immune-acquisition groups according to the breadth and magnitude of their antibody responses, suggesting that individual variation in the development of malaria immunity begins as early as first exposure. ConclusionsOur findings provide important insights into the immunogenicity of merozoite antigens under consideration for vaccine development and identify antigens that could be used in the development of malaria sero-surveillance tools.

papers.title: Epigenome-Wide Association Study of the Upper-Airway Microbiome Involved in Asthma Exacerbations
papers.abstract: RationaleThe role of DNA methylation (DNAm) markers in the upper-airway microbiome related to asthma exacerbations despite inhaled corticosteroid (ICS) treatment is unexplored. ObjectivesTo identify whole-blood DNAm markers associated with the upper-airway microbiome related to asthma exacerbations despite ICS treatment. MethodsWe analyzed salivary, nasal, and pharyngeal microbiome in 242 asthma patients (GEMAS) for discovery. We tested associations between whole-blood DNAm at 703,505 CpGs and 21 exacerbation-related microbiome traits. Replication for the nasal microbiome was evaluated in 272 (Project Viva) and 66 (SysPharmPediA) children with and without asthma. We analyzed differentially methylated regions (DMRs), gene enrichment, associations with blood gene expression (RNA-seq, n=119), and DNAm predictors of plasma proteins. Measurements and Main ResultsWhole-blood DNAm at 73 CpGs and 550 DMRs was associated with 17 exacerbation-related microbiome traits (false discovery rate [FDR]<0.05), including genes implicated in immune and inflammatory responses and the 17q12-q21 asthma locus ORMDL3. Most CpGs were associated with Campylobacter (pharyngeal) and Leptotrichia (nasal) abundance. Ten DNAm markers were replicated (p<0.05), including the corticosteroid insensitivity-related gene PTPRR associated with nasal bacterial richness. Enrichment analyses identified genes related to diabetes, obesity, smoking, TGF-{beta}, MAPK, and Wnt signaling and regulated by trichostatin A, NF-{kappa}B, and the glucocorticoid receptor (FDR<0.05). The CpG cg18994033, associated with pharyngeal Tannerella, was associated with ITM2C whole-blood expression. Nine DNAm-predicted plasma proteins involved in inflammation, tissue remodeling, and TGF-{beta} signaling were associated with seven exacerbation-related microbiome traits, including Streptococcus and Selenomonas. ConclusionsWhole-blood DNAm markers implicated in inflammation, immunity, and asthma comorbidities were associated with the upper-airway microbiome linked to asthma exacerbations.

papers.title: Patient Trajectories from Electronic Health Records Suggest Specialty Specific Warning Signs for Common Variable Immunodeficiency
papers.abstract: BackgroundCommon variable immunodeficiency is frequently underrecognized due to its heterogeneous clinical presentation, resulting in diagnostic delays that increase disease-related complications, with each year of delay increasing mortality risk by 4% for the most common inborn error of immunity. ObjectiveIn individuals with established common variable immunodeficiency, we sought to recognize patterns in patient diagnostic trajectories to identify opportunities for interventions to reduce time to diagnosis. MethodsWe analyzed retrospective electronic health records data from 139 individuals with physician-confirmed common variable immunodeficiency across five academic health systems representing >10million patients. We evaluated diagnosing specialties and international classification of disease code trajectories in the two years prior to and at common variable immunodeficiency confirmation. Additionally, we construct specialty-specific prediction on a 1:50 case: control cohort using a gradient boosting algorithm. ResultsThe leading diagnoses at common variable immunodeficiency determination were respiratory (35% of individuals), and individuals with respiratory symptoms were more likely to be diagnosed by Allergy / Immunology than by other specialties (odds ratio 2.9, standard error 0.35, p-value 1.9x10-3) and had a higher frequency of visits to pulmonary disease in the two years prior to diagnosis. Individuals with neoplasms were 50% more likely than other patients (OR 2.0, SE 0.29, p-value 0.02) to receive a diagnosis at each visit, reducing their diagnostic delay by up to a year. We find that a larger ratio of number of specialties visited to the total number of visits is significantly correlated with an increased time to diagnosis. A trajectory-informed specialty-specific prediction improved detection with an area under the precision-recall curve of fifty times the value expected under the null. ConclusionsIndividuals referred to Allergy / Immunology have shorter time to diagnosis, and a specialty-specific prediction could improve detection of common variable immunodeficiency. Clinical ImplicationsOverall, we find that phenotype-specialty interactions may inform targeted interventions to improve common variable immunodeficiency recognition across specialties, reducing diagnostic odyssey and disease-related complications. Capsule SummarySpecialty-specific symptom patterns and patient trajectories preceding common variable immunodeficiency diagnosis reveal opportunities for earlier recognition through context-aware electronic health record-based prediction.

papers.title: Multi-omics approach to map a clinically diverse large cohort with homozygous founder RAG1 p.C176F variant among Old Order Mennonites
papers.abstract: Partially preserved function of recombination-activating genes (RAG) 1 and 2 can be linked to divergent and hard-to-predict clinical and immunological phenotypes, even among close relatives. It is unclear how intrinsic RAG hypomorphism interacts with extrinsic environmental pressures to shape clinical trajectory. We dissect this phenomenon in a unique cohort of 18 Old Order Mennonite individuals with a novel missense founder RAG1 variant (p.C176F) with 25.8% recombinase activity of wild-type protein. After studying a myriad of markers, we demonstrate varying severity and progression of clinical disease (predominantly in females) that paralleled decline in CMV-specific immune competence, break in tolerance with hallmark presence of antibodies to IFN, a TH1/IFN{gamma}-driven inflammatory milieu with elevated serum markers (CXCL9/10), expansion of follicular helper T cells and clonal B cells enriched for autoreactive-prone VH4.34 B cell receptor. BCR and TCR repertoires carry the fingerprints of both extrinsic and RAG-driven intrinsic changes. Through this experiment of nature, our cohort demonstrated that partial RAG deficiency (pRD) is not a monolithic disease but the result of compounded RAG intrinsic and extrinsic events. Overall, this study uses multi-omics approaches to dissect the contribution of a hypomorphic RAG variant to variable severity of clinical disease and immunological dysregulation at cellular and molecular level. Emerging biomarkers of a multi-omic roadmap should allow monitoring of progression of clinical disease and guide who and when to treat with hematopoietic stem cell transplant in pRD. One sentence summaryA unique cohort of pediatric and adult US Mennonite patients with shared novel partial RAG defect and variable penetrance of disease allow correlation of clinical severity with RAG-intrinsic and extrinsic factors driving plasticity in T and B cell competence to eliminate infections and tolerance to self.

papers.title: Blood epigenetic remodeling in asthma associated with biologic therapy
papers.abstract: BackgroundPolygenic risk scores (PRS) capture inherited susceptibility to asthma, whereas methylation risk scores (MRS) may reflect disease-associated epigenetic variation. We assessed whether these scores differ in patients requiring biologic therapy and whether MRS change after mepolizumab initiation. MethodsCross-sectional analyses in the GEMAS study included 699 participants with genotype data (428 with asthma, 271 controls) and 668 with blood DNA methylation data (408 with asthma, 260 controls). We evaluated 35 existing asthma PRS and derived six MRS from published epigenomic asthma studies. Longitudinal MRS changes after mepolizumab initiation were assessed in 16 GEMAS patients and were replicated in 20 patients from the MEGA study. ResultsTwenty-eight PRS differentiated biologic-treated patients from controls (areas under the curve [AUC], 0.68-0.75), but none distinguished biologic-treated and non-treated patients after multiple-testing correction. MRS was higher in asthma without biologic than in controls (odds ratio [OR], 1.64; 95% CI, 1.34-1.99) and lower in biologic-treated than in asthma without biologic patients (OR, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.35-0.81). MRS did not differ significantly between biologic-treated patients and controls. Following mepolizumab initiation, MRS decreased at 6 and 12 months in GEMAS (p=4.81x10-5 and p=2.40x10-5, respectively). The 6-month decrease was also observed in MEGA (p=3.25x10-9). MRS epigenetic markers were predominantly hypermethylated, opposite to their described pattern in asthma risk. ConclusionsAsthma PRS did not differ significantly between biologic-treated and non-biologic-treated patients, but asthma MRS were lower in biologic-treated patients. The MRS decreased after mepolizumab initiation in two independent cohorts, consistent with a reversal of asthma-associated epigenetic patterns.

papers.title: Experimental model of VZV reactivation reveals vaccine-induced mechanisms of protection against herpes zoster
papers.abstract: Herpes zoster (HZ), caused by varicella zoster virus (VZV) reactivation, is common in older adults with declining cell-mediated immune protection. A modestly efficacious live attenuated (ZVL) and a highly efficacious recombinant adjuvanted (RZV) zoster vaccine protect against HZ. To uncover the mechanism(s) associated with the superior efficacy of RZV, we developed a controlled human infection model consisting of intradermal administration of attenuated vOka VZV to older adults previously vaccinated with RZV or ZVL. Infiltration of VZV-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cell clonotypes at the infection site was quicker and higher in RZV than ZVL recipients [≥]5 years post-immunization due to the persistence of RZV-induced gE-reactive CD4+ and CD8+ T cell clonotypes in blood. High CD4+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte frequencies in blood on Day 1 post-inoculation predicted control of VZV replication. Persistence of circulating RZV-induced CD4+ and CD8+ CTL and rapid migration to sites of VZV replication are potential mechanisms underlying durable protection against HZ.

papers.title: An altered B cell compartment distinguishes low antibody responders among people with HIV
papers.abstract: Chronic HIV infection can leave persistent immune dysregulation despite effective antiretroviral therapy (ART), but how this altered immune landscape affects antibody induction and durability after antigen exposure remains unclear. We used SARS-CoV-2 infection and vaccination as a model of humoral immunity to a novel antigen, evaluating anti-RBD IgG titers and immune cell phenotypes in people with HIV (PWH) and without HIV (PWoH) with hybrid immunity, stratified by early (<90 days) or late ([≥]90 days) post-exposure time points. PWH who failed to mount protective anti-RBD IgG titers early had a B cell compartment that was distinct from PWoH and high-titer PWH. Specifically, low-titer PWH had the highest expansion of activated naive, CD11c age-associated, and IgM-skewed B cells with reduced regulatory marker expression, even after controlling for age, sex, BMI and days since infection. PWH who had low-titer responses during the late phase of the response had persistent CD11c-associated features with expansion of double-negative and altered class-switched memory B cell compartments. These B cell features correlated with CD4 and CD8 T cell activation and senescence-associated phenotypes, suggesting that failure to mount high titer antibody response and maintenance in a subset of PWH is shaped by coordinated immune dysregulation.

papers.title: Human inherited RORγT deficiency encompasses genetic heterogeneity, T cell deficiency, and clinical homogeneity
papers.abstract: We previously reported inherited ROR{gamma}T deficiency in seven patients from three ancestries (Chilean, Palestinian, Saudi Arabian) with mycobacterial disease and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis (CMC). We report here five additional patients from different ancestries (Afghan, Indian, Iranian, Japanese, Sri Lankan), each homozygous for a new loss-of-function RORC variant. All but one patient -- the exception receiving early prophylaxis -- developed mycobacterial disease due to a near-complete depletion of innate-like adaptive T cells, including MAIT and iNKT cells, low counts of adaptive TH1* and CD8+ T cells, and impaired Mycobacterium-induced IFN-{gamma} production by the remaining cells of these subsets, NK cells, conventional CD4+ T, V{delta}1, and V{delta}2 {gamma}{delta}T cells. Most patients also displayed CMC due to their low counts of TH17 and TH1* cells. One patient died from disseminated Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccine infection, but, unexpectedly, all the other patients are still alive and clinically stable. ROR{gamma}T is essential for protective immunity against mycobacteria and Candida in humans.

papers.title: Human milk short-chain fatty acid concentrations are not associated with early childhood allergic disease
papers.abstract: BackgroundShort-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are microbial metabolites with immunoregulatory properties. Human milk contains SCFAs which have been proposed as potential modulators of infant immune development. We aimed to examine associations between human milk SCFA concentrations and infant allergic disease outcomes in a high-risk cohort of infants of atopic mothers. MethodsSCFAs were measured by targeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry in human milk samples collected at 3 and 6 months postpartum from atopic mothers enrolled in the Infant Fish Oil Supplementation (IFOS) Study (n=147). Associations between milk SCFA concentrations and early childhood allergic disease outcomes (atopic dermatitis, food allergy, allergic rhinitis, and allergen sensitisation at 1 and 2-3 years) were examined using logistic regression. ResultsHuman milk SCFA concentrations were broadly stable between 3 and 6 months postpartum, except for acetate which was significantly elevated at 6 months. No significant associations were observed between human milk SCFA concentrations and any allergic disease outcome after correction for multiple comparisons (all p>0.05). ConclusionsHuman milk SCFA concentrations are not associated with allergic disease outcomes up to 4 years of age. These findings suggest that oral SCFA exposure via human milk is insufficient to reduce infant allergy risk, and that gut SCFA production may be a more relevant target for future allergy prevention research.

papers.title: Autoantibodies From Connective Tissue Diseases Penetrate Cells and Exert Functional Properties
papers.abstract: Antinuclear antibodies (ANAs) are a hallmark of connective tissue diseases (CTDs) and serve as robust diagnostic biomarkers. Because their cognate antigens are intracellular, ANAs have long been considered non-pathogenic in CTDs. Here, using systemic sclerosis (SSc) associated anti-topoisomerase I antibodies (ATAs) as a model, we provide data challenging this view. We show that ANAs enter living cells, accumulate in nuclei, and engage their intracellular antigen. Nuclear ATAs inhibit topoisomerase I enzymatic activity, induces DNA damage, fibrosis, and, through the STING pathway, activates type I interferon production. We further identify neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)-dependent intracellular trafficking as a key determinant of ANAs nuclear access and demonstrate that pharmacological FcRn blockade impairs ATAs functionality. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized intracellular effector function of ANAs and establish a mechanistic framework by which ANAs may directly contribute to tissue injury in CTDs.

papers.title: Post-vaccination expansion of extrafollicular Th10 and regulatory Tfr cells distinguishes strong from weak influenza vaccine responses in older adults
papers.abstract: Despite the superior efficacy of high-dose influenza vaccines, over one-third of older adults fail to respond. Yet, the mechanisms underlying this impaired vaccine responsiveness remain poorly understood. Here, we performed longitudinal profiling of older adults (n=60) receiving high-dose influenza vaccination to identify immune programs associated with vaccine responsiveness. Strong responders exhibited a primed baseline immune state characterized by elevated plasma cytokines and chemokines, followed by enhanced IFN-{gamma} responses and coordinated transcriptional and epigenetic activation of cDC2 cells at day 1. By day 7, CD4 T-cell trajectories diverged: strong responders preferentially expanded influenza-specific activated cTfh1 (CXCR5+ CXCR3+ ICOS+ CD38+) and influenza-specific Th10 (CXCR5- CXCR3+ PD1+ IL10) cells, whereas weak responders expanded regulatory cTfr (CXCR5 FOXP3) cells. Th10 expansion correlated with plasmablast and antibody responses and was independently validated in a larger influenza vaccination cohort, including younger adults. Functionally, Th10 cells promoted memory B-cell differentiation into plasmablasts and production of influenza-specific IgGs. TCR analyses revealed minimal clonal overlap between Th10 and cTfh1 cells. Together, these findings identify divergent helper and regulatory CD4 T cell programs associated with vaccine responsiveness and establish Th10 cells as a previously unrecognized component of vaccine-induced humoral immunity.

papers.title: Gut microbiome signatures associated with self-reported allergic symptoms among Finnish adults
papers.abstract: BackgroundGrowing evidence suggests that the gut microbiome influences nasal and ocular allergic inflammation through gut-mucosal immune interactions. Yet, its association with Allergic rhinitis (AR) and allergic eye symptoms (AES) remains incompletely understood in large population-based cohorts. ObjectiveTo examine associations between the gut microbiome and self-reported AR and AES in Finnish adults. MethodsShallow metagenomic sequencing was performed on stool samples from a population-based cohort (FINRISK02; n = 7,231). Microbial taxonomic and functional profiles were compared between individuals with AR (n = 1,950), AES (n = 1,554), combined allergies (AR and/or AES; n = 2,305), and controls without reported symptoms (n = 3,175). ResultsAllergic groups exhibited lower microbial richness and phylogenetic diversity than controls. Shared microbial and functional signatures were observed across AR and AES, consistent with their high co-occurrence (N = 1,199). Compared with controls, allergic groups showed enrichment of 17 bacterial species, predominantly from the Clostridia class, including taxa previously associated with asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and atopic dermatitis. Allergic individuals also exhibited enrichment of pathways related to mucosal carbohydrate processing, shikimate metabolism, histidine turnover, and broader amino acid metabolism. Concurrent enrichment of histidine biosynthesis and degradation suggested altered microbial histidine metabolism. ConclusionsAdult allergic symptoms are associated with gut microbiome taxonomic and functional alterations linked to mucosal barrier function and immune-related metabolism, supporting a shared gut-mucosal immune axis across allergic phenotypes. Clinical ImplicationShared microbial signatures across AR and AES support the concept of a common gut-mucosal immune axis underlying allergic manifestations in adults. Capsule SummaryThe large population-based study revealed that allergic symptoms in adults are associated with lower richness and phylogenetic diversity of gut microbiome together with taxonomic and functional alterations

papers.title: Inherited human TFIIIA deficiency disrupts T cell development
papers.abstract: Molecular characterization of human monogenic inborn errors of T cell immunity provides both biological insights and medical progress. We report rare biallelic deleterious variants in GTF3A, encoding transcription factor IIIA (TFIIIA), a zinc-finger protein required for transcription and chaperoning of 5S ribosomal RNA (rRNA). These variants were identified in ten patients from eight unrelated families and eight countries presenting with either T-B+NK+ severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) or combined immune deficiency (CID), characterized by T cell lymphopenia and variable antibody deficiency. The GTF3A variants disrupt TFIIIA function through distinct mechanisms, including defective DNA binding, aberrant nuclear localization, and reduced protein stability compromising TFIIIA-mediated transcription and chaperoning of 5S rRNA. Using artificial thymic organoids derived from TFIIIA-deficient CD34 progenitors, an early developmental arrest at the T cell commitment stage was documented in vitro. Zebrafish deficient for gtf3aa recapitulated the impaired thymocyte development in vivo. Together, these findings establish TFIIIA deficiency as a novel cause of (S)CID, expanding the genetic and mechanistic landscape of inborn errors of T cell immunity and uncovering an essential role for TFIIIA in human adaptive immunity. One-sentence summaryBiallelic GTF3A variants causing TFIIIA deficiency, which disrupts 5S rRNA transcription, represent a novel monogenic cause of (S)CID, unveiling a crucial role of TFIIIA in T cell development.
